candidate_ideas.statement: The exclusion of balanced CE relations on a genus-six hyperelliptic degree-four cover needs neither an explicit curve model nor the CE relative-canonical normalization: for γ=q∘h, E=O(1)⊕O(4)^2 is forced for every degree-2 map q; then h^0(Sym^2E(-6))=9 while h^0(C,O_{P(E^∨)}(2)|_C⊗γ^*O(-6))=7 follows from degree alone (deg=12>2g-2=10), and left-exactness gives h^0(F(-6))≥2, excluding splitting types (4,5) and (3,6) among a+b=9.

On a balanced fibre satisfying the weak CE normalization, h^0(L)=3 together with base-point-freeness of L on the balanced locus makes a general member of |L|≅P^2 consist of six distinct points, so the reduced-support open of the closed Abel–Jacobi incidence is nonempty and dense in every fibre of the P^2-bundle (a base point would yield a g^2_5 and a smooth plane quintic whose tetragonal pencil is CE-unbalanced; characteristic-zero Bertini then yields six distinct points).

established_facts.statement: For a degree-four Casnati–Ekedahl cover, deg(W_f|_C)=4g+12-4f; at g=6 and f=5 one has deg(W_5)=16 and deg(L)=deg(W_5⊗ω_C^{-1})=6.

On every smooth genus-6 fibre of a balanced tetragonal CE family, with M:=ω_C^2⊗W_5^∨ and L:=W_5⊗ω_C^{-1}, one has deg M=2(2g-2)-(4g+12-4f)|_{g=6,f=5}=20-16=4 and h^0(L)=1+h^0(M) from χ(L)=1 plus Serre duality.

On every such fibre M is always special (h^1(M)=h^0(L)≥1); Clifford gives h^0(M)≤deg(M)/2+1=3 with equality only for hyperelliptic C and M≅(g^1_2)^{⊗2} (since deg M=4∉{0,2g-2}), so h^0(L)∈{1,2,3,4}, never 5, and h^0(L)=4 occurs only on hyperelliptic fibres.
Granting the weak CE relative-canonical normalization O_{P(E^∨)}(1)|_C≅ω_{C/P^1}⊗γ^*A for some line bundle A on P^1, degree forces A≅O_{P^1}, hence W_5≅ω_C^2(-D), L≅ω_C(-D), and M≅O_C(D)≅γ^*O(1).

Under that normalization, h^0(M)≥2 (γ^* injective on H^0(P^1,O(1))) and h^0(M)≤3 by Clifford, so h^0(L)∈{3,4} on balanced fibres; equivalently, constancy of h^0(L)=3 on the balanced locus is the same as absence of a balanced fibre whose tetragonal pencil factors through a degree-two map.

For a line bundle L of relative degree d on a smooth proper curve family C/B, the functor of relative effective divisors Γ with O(Γ)≅L is represented by the closed Abel–Jacobi fibre Sym^d(C/B)×_{Pic^d(C/B)}B (=Hilb^d on a smooth curve); this agrees with Proj(π_*L) precisely over the open where h^0(L) is constant.

Constant geometric-fibre dimensions of a perfect two-term complex do not by themselves yield locally free cohomology or arbitrary base change over a nonreduced base; a separate constant-rank or lifting argument is required.
